title: Area Architects II
goal: I can find the area and the perimeter of shapes with square corners. I can compare rectangles with the same area.

learn.intro: Area is the space inside a shape, in cm². Perimeter is the distance round the edge, in cm. For a shape with square corners, take a piece away from a big rectangle, or split it into rectangles.

example.problem: The shape has square corners. Find its area and its perimeter.
steps: Big rectangle: 10 × 6 = 60. The missing corner is 4 × 2 = 8. Area = 60 − 8 = 52.
Push the steps out to make a rectangle. The perimeter is 10 + 6 + 10 + 6 = 32.

example2.problem: Rectangles with whole-cm sides have an area of 18 cm². Find the perimeter of each one.
steps: List the pairs that multiply to 18 in order: 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6.
example2.answer: The smallest perimeter is 18 cm, from 6 cm by 3 cm.

howto.title: How to do it
steps: Missing sides: use the opposite sides.
Area: split into rectangles, or take a piece away.
Perimeter: push the steps out to a rectangle.

try.text: A rectangle is 12 cm long and 5 cm wide. A 3 cm by 2 cm corner is cut off. What is the area of the shape that is left? {b} cm²
try.explanation: The rectangle has an area of 12 × 5 = 60 cm². The corner has an area of 3 × 2 = 6 cm². 60 − 6 = 54 cm².

items.text: The shape has square corners. Find the missing sides a and b. Then find the area and the perimeter.

parts.label: a
parts.text: a = {b} cm   b = {b} cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: Area: {b} cm²

parts.label: c
parts.text: Perimeter: {b} cm

items.explanation: (a) a = 11 − 7 = 4 cm and b = 8 − 3 = 5 cm. (b) Split: 11 × 3 + 7 × 5 = 68 cm². Or 11 × 8 − 4 × 5 = 68 cm². (c) Push the steps out: 2 × (11 + 8) = 38 cm.

items.text: A 12 cm by 9 cm rectangle has a corner cut off. The corner is shown with a dashed line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Area of the whole rectangle: {b} cm²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Area of the corner cut off: {b} cm²

parts.label: c
parts.text: Area of the shape left: {b} cm²

items.explanation: (a) 12 × 9 = 108 cm². (b) The corner is 5 cm by 4 cm: 5 × 4 = 20 cm². (c) 108 − 20 = 88 cm².

items.text: Every rectangle here has whole-cm sides and covers 28 cm². Fill in the table. The length is the greater side.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Fill in the table.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The least perimeter is {b} cm

items.explanation: 28 ÷ 28 = 1, 28 ÷ 14 = 2 and 28 ÷ 7 = 4. The perimeters are 2 × (28 + 1) = 58, 2 × (14 + 2) = 32 and 2 × (7 + 4) = 22. The least is 22 cm, from the shape that is nearest to a square.

items.text: Each shape is made of 5 square tiles that are each 1 cm by 1 cm. The tiles touch along whole sides.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The area of each shape: {b} cm²

parts.label: b
parts.text: The perimeters of A, B and C: {b} cm, {b} cm, {b} cm

parts.label: c
parts.text: The shape with the least perimeter is {circ:A|B|C}

items.explanation: Each shape has 5 tiles, so the area is 5 cm². Count the edges. A: 10 cm. B: 5 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 12 cm. C: 12 cm. A is the most compact, so it has the least perimeter.

items.text: The staircase has 4 equal steps. Each step is 3 cm across and 2 cm high.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Perimeter: {b} cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: Area: {b} cm²

items.explanation: (a) Push the steps out to a 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle: 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 cm. (b) The rows are 12, 9, 6 and 3 cm long and 2 cm high: 2 × 30 = 60 cm².

items.text: A lawn is 16 m long and 10 m wide. A square pond with sides of 4 m sits in the lawn.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Area of lawn, not pond: {b} m²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Both edges together: {b} m

items.explanation: (a) The lawn is 16 × 10 = 160 m². The pond is 4 × 4 = 16 m². 160 − 16 = 144 m². (b) The lawn edge is 2 × (16 + 10) = 52 m. The pond edge is 4 × 4 = 16 m. 52 + 16 = 68 m.

items.text: Cut a 10 cm by 3 cm strip on the dashed line. Join the 2 pieces to make a 5 cm by 6 cm rectangle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The area of the strip is {b} cm² and the area of the rectangle is {b} cm².

parts.label: b
parts.text: The perimeter of the strip is {b} cm and of the rectangle is {b} cm.

items.explanation: (a) 10 × 3 = 30 cm² and 5 × 6 = 30 cm². Moving pieces does not change the area. (b) Strip: 2 × (10 + 3) = 26 cm. Rectangle: 2 × (5 + 6) = 22 cm. The perimeter changed.

items.text: A rectangle has an area of 72 cm². Its length is 9 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Its width is {b} cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: Its perimeter is {b} cm

items.text: A hall floor is 12 m long and 8 m wide. It is covered with square tiles that are each 2 m by 2 m.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many tiles cover the floor? {b} tiles

parts.label: b
parts.text: The tiles along the edge are dark. How many tiles are dark? {b} tiles

items.explanation: (a) 12 ÷ 2 = 6 tiles along the length and 8 ÷ 2 = 4 tiles along the width. 6 × 4 = 24 tiles. (b) The tiles not along the edge make a block of 4 by 2 = 8 tiles. 24 − 8 = 16 dark tiles.

items.text: A rectangle has a perimeter of 42 cm. Its length is 5 cm more than its width. What is its area? {b} cm²
items.hint: Length + width is half of the perimeter.
items.explanation: Half of the perimeter is length + width = 21 cm. The length is 5 more than the width, so 21 − 5 = 16 cm is 2 widths. The width is 8 cm and the length is 13 cm: 13 × 8 = 104 cm².

items.text: Three squares have areas of 4 cm², 9 cm² and 16 cm². They stand side by side on one line, as shown. Find the perimeter of the whole shape. {b} cm
items.hint: Find the side of each square first.
items.explanation: The sides are 2, 3 and 4 cm. Push the steps out: the shape fits in a 9 cm by 4 cm rectangle with the same perimeter, 2 × (9 + 4) = 26 cm.

items.text: Two identical rectangles are each 8 cm long and 3 cm wide. They are joined along a whole side to make one bigger rectangle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Joined along an 8 cm side, the perimeter is {b} cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: Joined along a 3 cm side, the perimeter is {b} cm

items.hint: Draw both. Find the length and width of each big rectangle.
items.explanation: (a) The big rectangle is 8 cm by 6 cm: 2 × 14 = 28 cm. (b) The big rectangle is 16 cm by 3 cm: 2 × 19 = 38 cm.

items.text:
Three identical squares are joined in an L shape. The perimeter of the L shape is 40 cm. Find its area.
{b} cm²
items.hint: Count the sides of squares round the edge of the L shape.
items.explanation: The edge of the L shape has 8 sides of squares. 40 ÷ 8 = 5 cm for 1 side. Each square has an area of 5 × 5 = 25 cm², so the L shape has 3 × 25 = 75 cm².

items.text:
Take a square with sides of 4 cm. Its area is 16 cm² and its perimeter is 16 cm. The numbers match! Find 1 other rectangle with whole-cm sides where they match.
Length {b} cm   Width {b} cm
items.hint: Try a width of 1, then 2, then 3. Does the area equal the perimeter?
items.explanation: Width 3, length 6: area 18 cm² and perimeter 2 × 9 = 18 cm. Width 1 or 2 never works (width 2 gives 2l and 2l + 4). Widths of 4 or more give only the 4 by 4 square. So 6 cm by 3 cm.

items.text: Two squares with sides of 6 cm overlap at one corner. The overlap is a square with sides of 2 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Area of the whole shape: {b} cm²

parts.label: b
parts.text: Perimeter of the whole shape: {b} cm

items.hint: The overlap is part of both squares.
items.explanation: (a) 36 + 36 = 72, but the 2 by 2 overlap is counted twice: 72 − 4 = 68 cm². (b) Go round the edge: 6 + 4 + 4 + 6 + 6 + 4 + 4 + 6 = 40 cm.

items.text: A square floor is covered with square tiles. The tiles along the edge are dark and all the others are light.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The floor is 8 tiles by 8 tiles. How many dark tiles? {b}

parts.label: b
parts.text: A floor has 60 dark tiles. How many tiles long is the floor? {b}

items.hint: Take the light block away from the whole floor.
items.explanation: (a) The light tiles make a 6 by 6 block: 36. 64 − 36 = 28 dark tiles. (b) A floor n tiles long has 4 × n − 4 dark tiles. 4 × n − 4 = 60 gives n = 16.

items.text: Find the area of the shape. {b} cm²
A rectangle has an area of 60 cm² and a length of 12 cm. Find its perimeter. {b} cm
items.explanation: The width is 60 ÷ 12 = 5 cm. The perimeter is 2 × (12 + 5) = 34 cm.

items.text: A 10 cm by 7 cm photo has a frame 1 cm wide on every side. Find the area of the frame alone. {b} cm²
items.explanation: The whole is 12 cm by 9 cm = 108 cm². The photo is 10 × 7 = 70 cm². 108 − 70 = 38 cm².

items.text: Every rectangle has whole-cm sides and covers 24 cm². Find the least perimeter any of them can have. {b} cm
items.explanation: The pairs are 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8 and 4 × 6, with perimeters 50, 28, 22 and 20. The least is 20 cm, from 4 cm by 6 cm.
